title: Case-Sensitive WebSocket Upgrade Check Bypass in Admin API
analysis:
The administrative API performs a check to block browser-initiated WebSocket connections because WebSockets are not protected by typical Same-Origin Policy (SOP) / CORS restrictions. However, the check `strings.Contains(r.Header.Get("Upgrade"), "websocket")` is case-sensitive. Since HTTP `Upgrade` header values are case-insensitive, an attacker or browser can send `Upgrade: WebSocket` or `Upgrade: WEBSOCKET`, which bypasses this check. If `enforceOrigin` is not configured, this bypass can expose the admin API to Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH) and unauthorized request execution.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
GET /config/ HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:2019
Upgrade: WebSocket
Connection: Upgrade
Origin: http://attacker.com
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
```

This request bypasses the WebSocket upgrade check because 'WebSocket' does not contain 'websocket' (case-sensitively), letting the request reach the admin router.
vuln_type: CWE-178: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity
